close_reason: Resolved together with JMAP-826m.30. The new helper unhandled_backend_set_error(&e) at helpers.rs uses format!('unhandled backend error variant: {e:?}') so the variant name surfaces in the serverFail description. BackendSetError derives Debug (workspace foundation convention) so this is greppable in operator logs without source-code spelunking.
description:
metadata.rs:389-393, 453-457, 505-509: when BackendSetError gains a new variant the metadata-server doesn't know about, the response is:

  { "type": "serverFail", "description": "unhandled backend error variant" }

A client/operator sees this and has no information about which variant fired, what to do, or where to report it. The right thing is at least include the discriminant name (BackendSetError::CustomVariant or similar). Rust's Debug impl on BackendSetError can be invoked: format!("unhandled backend error variant: {e:?}") would surface the variant name.

Audience: operator triaging a serverFail in production. Currently they get the same string regardless of which variant fired.

What would make it clear: include the Debug repr of the error in the description. Per RFC 8620 §5.3 the description is non-localised and is debugging-grade — exactly the right channel for this info.
title: Error description 'unhandled backend error variant' for catch-all is not actionable — caller sees serverFail with no clue what variant fired
